newsitem.title: UK: Willis to trial new Lloyd's data system.
newsitem.headline: Willis to trial new Lloyd's data system.

text.p: Broker Willis Corroon Group Plc will next week begin testing a database aimed at speeding up business within Lloyd's of London, an insurance market spokesman told Reuters.
"The Holy Grail we're after here is a tool that helps people to do business," David Betts, manager of Insurance Services at Lloyd's, said on Thursday.

The aim of the Market Information Repository (MIR) is to collect all the data used by brokers and underwriters during the placing of a risk into one easily accessible database and reduce the insurance paper-chase.

The system can store information in many forms, including text, pictures, diagrams and spreadsheets. This can then be retrieved should there be a query or claim or at the renewal of a policy. Security systems will limit access to sensitive information.
"The whole thing makes huge sense. The reaction from brokers has been 'give it to me tomorrow and I could use it straightaway'," Betts said.
The test phase with Willis, several other brokers and Lloyd's underwriters will run until the year end, with production set for the first quarter of 1998.
Betts said MIR had been developed with easily available, low-cost, web-type technology, adding that alterations were not difficult to implement.
MIR has the support of LIMNET -- the London Insurance Market Network -- and should eventually be available to the whole London insurance market, Betts added.
LIMNET development manager Andy Edwards said he hoped MIR would also be used internationally as a data warehouse by companies outside the London Market.
MIR is a utility and not in competition with existing systems such as the World Insurance Network (WIN), which was launched last week.
"It's not a competitor to WIN. It's a building block for other people to build competitive services. Lloyd's is in this to help get business placed with Lloyd's underwriters," Betts said.
Willis is also one of the four backers of WIN, which has strong support from executive director Max Taylor, who was last week nominated to take over as chairman of Lloyd's in January 1998.
